QF.id: VIII Introduction to Forwards and Futures_111

question.text: On the last day before Nifty futures expiry, spot Nifty is at 25,000 and the futures are at 25,050. A trader notices this 50-point premium and is considering a cash-and-carry arbitrage. Per the NISM Series VIII workbook, before deciding whether the trade is profitable, what is the most important factor the trader must evaluate?

answer.text: Whether the 50-point premium covers all transaction costs (brokerage, STT, exchange charges, GST), margin funding cost, and the expected impact cost on the cash and futures legs - because the workbook treats cash-and-carry as profitable only when net of these costs
Whether SEBI permits arbitrage on the expiry day
Whether the trade can be executed only by institutional investors and not retail traders
Nothing - the 50-point premium is a guaranteed riskless profit and the trader should execute immediately

explanation.text: The Logic: The NISM Series VIII workbook (pp.44, 50, 56, 141-142) treats cash-and-carry arbitrage as viable only when the futures-spot basis exceeds all execution costs - brokerage, STT and exchange charges, GST, margin funding cost, and the impact cost on both the cash buy and the futures sell. Near expiry the cost of carry is negligible, so any premium is theoretically arbitrageable; but it is only realised profit if net of these costs. The keyed option captures exactly that principle. The Trap: Arbitrage is not prohibited near expiry, so the SEBI option is wrong. It is not restricted to institutions. The "guaranteed profit" option ignores transaction costs entirely. The audit flagged the original because the stem gave no cost assumptions, so a categorical "should not attempt" answer was not uniquely supportable from the workbook, and the prior explanation cited specific STT (0.1%) and rupee cost figures that the cached pages did not contain. Note: The original asked the trader to decide whether to attempt the arbitrage, but the cited workbook pages support a cost-analysis principle rather than a categorical yes/no for this fact set. The item has been rewritten as a principle question asking what the trader must evaluate, which the workbook directly supports, and the unsourced specific cost numbers have been removed.
